title: Power Automate: self-healing repairs desktop flow selector failures with AI
summary: Hold: the briefing incorrectly leaves the EU Data Boundary position unresolved, although Microsoft's provider guidance explicitly excludes Claude models deployed in Power Platform from those commitments. The roadmap facts, preview licensing and cited control paths are otherwise supported, with minor qualifications noted.

claims.claim: The roadmap modification timestamp is 2026-11-17T18:36:41.
Self-healing is an agentic AI fallback that improves desktop flow resilience by identifying the intended UI element and generating an alternative selector when a UI or web selector fails.
claims.quote: When an existing selector can no longer locate the intended UI element, Power Automate for desktop uses AI to identify the element and generate an alternative selector.

claims.claim: General availability is planned to add a flow-level opt-in that logs a working alternative selector without applying the fix at runtime.
claims.quote: the GA phase will additionally include a flow-level opt-in option to only log the alternative, working selector in case of an error, without applying the fix during runtime.

claims.claim: For a supported action's Element not found error, retry policy runs before self-healing, followed by Set variable / Run subflow rules and then Continue flow run / Throw error.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: A successful repair uses the generated selector at runtime and the flow continues.
claims.quote: If the repair succeeds, the flow continues. ... the AI-generated selector that was used at runtime.

claims.claim: Normal error handling resumes when a self-healing repair fails.
claims.quote: If it fails, normal error handling resumes.

claims.claim: Self-healing is a runtime-only capability.
claims.quote: Self-healing is a runtime-only capability.

claims.claim: Self-healing applies to console runs and attended and unattended cloud runs.
claims.quote: It applies to console and cloud (attended and unattended) runs

claims.claim: Self-healing has no effect during designer runs.
claims.quote: has no effect during designer runs.

claims.claim: Only specific UI and browser automation actions interacting with a single UI element support self-healing.
claims.quote: Is available only for specific UI and browser automation actions that interact with a single UI element (for example, clicking a button or selecting a checkbox).

claims.claim: Self-healing covers Element not found and Window not found errors.
claims.quote: Applies only to Element not found and Window not found errors. Element not found errors are captured in both primary and secondary screens, while Window not found errors are only captured when the window is found in the main screen.
claims.fix: Add to the supported-errors sentence: 'Element not found errors are captured on primary and secondary screens; Window not found errors are captured only when the window is found on the main screen.'

claims.claim: Window or screen handling and multi-element actions such as Drag and drop UI element in window are excluded.
claims.quote: Doesn't apply to window or screen handling actions, or actions that interact with multiple elements like 'Drag and drop UI element in window'.

claims.claim: The self-healing prerequisite enables the tenant Anthropic subprocessor in Microsoft 365 admin center at Copilot > Settings > AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors.
claims.quote: In Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Settings, and then select AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors. Enable the Anthropic provider as a subprocessor for your organization.
claims.fix: Keep the cited self-healing path, but add this note: 'The provider's own guidance also includes View all: Copilot > Settings > View all > AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/connect-to-ai-subprocessor.

claims.claim: The self-healing prerequisite allows Anthropic at environment or environment-group level through Power Platform admin center > Copilot > Settings > Power Platform > External models.
claims.quote: In Power Platform admin center, go to Copilot > Settings, and then under the Power Platform section, expand External models and enable Anthropic as a subprocessor at environment or environment group level.
claims.fix: Keep the self-healing path and add: 'The external models guidance also gives the environment path Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features, where the model provider setting is turned On or Off.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/allow-llm-generative-responses.
